en.headline: Man arrested over alleged HK$2.84 million school placement scam
en.dek: Police say a 51-year-old businessman claimed he could secure places at a North Point secondary school and later university entry for dozens of students.
body: A 51-year-old Hong Kong man has been arrested on suspicion of defrauding a mainland education consultant of about HK$2.84 million by claiming he could arrange secondary school places and guaranteed university admission.

According to police sources, the suspect, who has held positions in parent-teacher association circles, signed a contract with a 45-year-old woman on 1 March 2024. He allegedly promised 50 places at Kiangsu-Chekiang College in North Point and said students would later gain entry to universities in Hong Kong or Macau regardless of Diploma of Secondary Education results. Between April and July 2024 the consultant transferred roughly HK$2.84 million in 23 payments to a mainland bank account for application fees covering 37 students. None received offers from the school or universities, and contact with the man ceased.

The woman reported the matter in May. Officers first detained the man in May at a Hung Hom hotel and arrested him again on 29 July at Hong Kong International Airport as he prepared to leave the city. The case is being handled by Hung Hom District Crime Squad as fraud.

zh.headline: 訛稱提供學額保送大學 男子涉騙284萬元機場被捕
zh.dek: 警方指51歲商人聲稱可提供蘇浙公學學額及保證入讀港澳大學，收受內地升學顧問約284萬元。
body: 一名51歲本港男子涉嫌訛稱可安排中學學額及保證大學取錄，騙取內地升學顧問約284萬元，已被警方拘捕。
據了解，該名男子曾在家長教師會等組織擔任職務。他於2024年3月1日與一名45歲女子簽約，聲稱可提供50個北角蘇浙公學學額，並口頭承諾學生完成課程後，不論文憑試成績如何，都可保證入讀香港或澳門大學。女子其後在4月至7月期間分23次匯款共約284萬元至男子指定的內地銀行戶口，作為37名學生的申請費。其後學生並無收到任何取錄或邀請，男子亦失去聯絡。
女子於5月報案。警方5月曾在紅磡一間酒店大堂拘捕該男子，7月29日他準備離港時於香港國際機場再次被捕。案件列作詐騙，由紅磡警區重案組跟進。
